case.summary: This case was triggered by customer C09988 reporting an unauthorized online purchase of $59.67 on card C09988-K1 on December 11, 2016. The graph analysis showed a device fanout cluster where the exact same Windows Edge 16.0 device profile was used across multiple victim accounts within 48 hours, including connected cards C00854-K2, C06224-K2, and C09251-K1. The verdict is confirmed fraud with an initial and final fraud probability of 0.99, supported by a case-memory model score of 0.862 and a calibrated fraud rate of 65.1%. The system executed automated actions to create the case and monitor connected cards under rule R6, while card blocking is recommended pending approval under rule R2 and report filing is recommended pending approval under policy 3a and rule R6.

sar.narrative: Customer C09988 reported an unauthorized transaction on card C09988-K1 involving an online purchase of $59.67 that occurred on December 11, 2016 at 22:39:08. The transaction was conducted using a new device profile running Windows and Edge 16.0 with a hotmail.com email address. Investigation revealed that the same device profile was utilized in a tightly clustered series of online transactions across three other cards, specifically C00854-K2, C06224-K2, and C09251-K1, within a 48-hour window. This activity constitutes card-not-present fraud carried out via a shared device profile ring. The total exposure amount for this specific transaction is $59.67. The case-memory model assigned a score of 0.862, reflecting a calibrated fraud rate of 65.1%, and historical precedent confirms that all 4,665 cardholder-reported cases of this type in the bank's memory were confirmed fraud. Automated actions taken include creating the case and monitoring connected cards under rule R6, with card blocking recommended pending approval under rule R2 and report filing recommended pending approval under policy 3a and rule R6.
